brief: McElligott argues equities are in a rare 'Correlation 1' selloff: concentrated Mag7/AI positioning had kept dispersion high and index vol low, but a rethink in that positioning concentration is now pushing dispersion down and correlation (and index vol) up, with some rotation into defensives this morning meaning it is not yet outright capitulation. He reads this as an asset-allocation shift out of stocks into cash and USTs, driven by financial-conditions tightening (higher real rates, wider spreads, higher equity vol) producing a negative wealth effect on US consumers, NVDA's AI-financing optionality turning less favorable, a reset in AI capex trickle-down expectations, and a hawkish global central-bank stance meeting a possible supply shock. Separately, his alt-data model points to a negative December CPI print, raising policy-error risk as commodities melt down. USD rate vol is bid as Treasuries rally and the curve bull-steepens. He still flags mechanical catalysts (dealer short-covering, CTA trend flips, negative-gamma flows) for a near-term relief rally, but doubts it given crowded positioning in that call, and says failure to rally would signal a real growth scare and forced deleveraging by levered funds and retail allocators out of equities.
